:::{#exm-weibull-log-linear}
#### Median event times from the log-linear form

Take $\lambda = 0.1$ and $p = 2$,
so $\alpha = -\logf{0.1} = \logf{10} \approx 2.3026$ and $\sigma = 0.5$.
The median of $W$ solves $\expf{-\ef{w}} = 0.5$,
so $\ef{w} = \logf{2}$ and $w = \logf{\logf{2}} \approx -0.3665$.
Because $\alpha - \sigma \eta + \sigma W$ is an increasing function of $W$,
the median of $Y$ is that function evaluated at the median of $W$.

For a baseline subject ($\eta = 0$):

$$
\ba
\text{median}(Y)
&= \alpha + \sigma \cdot (-0.3665)
&& \text{(log-linear form at the median of } W \text{)} \\
&= 2.3026 - 0.1833
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&= 2.1193
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

so the median event time is $\ef{2.1193} \approx 8.33$.
Directly, $\surv_0(8.33) = \expf{-(0.833)^2} = \expf{-0.694} \approx 0.5$.

For a subject with hazard ratio $\theta = 4$, so $\eta = \logf{4} \approx 1.3863$,
the median of $Y$ shifts by $-\sigma \eta = -0.5 \cdot 1.3863 \approx -0.6931$,
so the median event time is multiplied by $\ef{-0.6931} = 0.5$,
giving $8.33 \cdot 0.5 \approx 4.16$.
:::
